It's Far Cry 5 with loot, vampires and odd graphics (seriously, the people look weird). If that sounds fun to you, check it out. It's nowhere near as bad as the internet dog-piling would have everyone believe. I've had a lot of fun exploring Redfall.

Redfall is an open world FPS featuring both single player and co-op modes. Starting the game, you can choose between four playable characters, each one with their unique abilities. The game is set in the town of Redfall (Massachusetts, US) during a vampire apocalypse that blocked the sun and caused the waters to recede. As one of the few remaining survivors, you will fight against multiple vampire Lords while investigating their appearance and trying to break the island’s curse. Unlike zombies, there aren’t many games featuring vampires, so it certainly feels refreshing to play one (while we patiently wait for [i]VTM Bloodlines 2[/i]). The setting often reminded me of [i]Salem’s Lot[/i] and the more recent [i]Midnight Mass[/i], which I love. Unfortunately, the story of Redfall is not engaging due to the lack of interesting secondary characters & antagonists. Cutscenes are like cheap static images from a storyboard showing how the real cutscenes should have been, if they were really made. I can’t understand how they let this happen and, considering the AAA increased price, this is totally unacceptable. Main quests are decent enough thanks to the variety of locations, while secondary ones are the classic “go there and find this item” or “go there and kill this enemy”. Keep in mind that completing some secondary quests is also mandatory for unlocking the final main quest, in case you are thinking of simply rushing through the story. You can’t replay any completed quest, so right now some achievements can only be obtained if you make one or two more playthroughs or if you are lucky enough to play the same mission differently through co-op.

The gunplay has been improved thanks to the collaboration with ID Software. While still not perfect, it feels smoother than any previous Arkane game. There is decent variety in weapons too, ranging from pistols and shotguns to flareguns and stake launchers. Each weapon can be customized with different skins and has a level or rarity in the following order: white, green, blue, purple and orange. Unfortunately, you won’t find any unique weapons and you will often swap between the same ones with different levels. For some weird reason there are no throwables, such as grenades or molotov. The game’s tutorial tells you that stealth is also an option, yet it feels really bad, like there isn’t even an animation for the silent takedown and you just punch human enemies in the back hoping they will instantly die (sometimes they don’t). Enemies are not very varied and you will often fight vampires, gangs of human cultists and mercenary soldiers, who also tend to fight each other. Their AI is one of the worst I have ever seen and completely ruins the combat experience. Enemies often stand still and stare at you or look in the wrong direction even when you are shooting at them; they have incredibly slow reaction times so you can kill them easily. Even the final bosses are affected, with Jacob’s invisibility power capable of breaking their AI as it continuously swaps between normal mode and combat mode.

If you played [i]Dishonored[/i], [i]Prey[/i] or [i]Deathloop[/i], you know that level design is what Arkane makes best. Redfall’s environments are fascinating to explore, buildings can be accessed in multiple ways, interiors are greatly detailed, particularly the ones connected to main missions. Level design is what kept me playing the game, wanting to know what I could find inside the lighthouse I saw from the distance, inside a hidden cave or a giant mansion heavily guarded. It’s a pity that the rest of the game doesn’t have the same quality. While Arkane said the game was perfectly playable as a single player (and that is true), the experience is built around co-op, so it’s not really much fun alone. Characters are meant to compensate each other and while playing as Jacob, who is a stealth hero with the abilities of detecting enemies behind walls, becoming invisible for a short time and instantly sniping everyone, I realized I could use some more offensive abilities to make combat more varied and engaging. Despite being alone, characters and enemies often refer to you as a group of people, fast travelling starts a 5-second countdown, missions must be accepted in a briefing room so you must always fast travel to your HQ to start them. All this was clearly designed for co-op, yet for some reason there is no public matchmaking, meaning you need to have friends who are willing to spend this amount of money to buy the game and invite them to your lobby. Even then, only the host maintains the story progression while the other players can only keep the experience and gear collected, so when they return to their world they must play the story missions again. I think this was a terrible mistake and that Arkane should have just copied [i]Borderlands[/i], where you can join public lobbies and skip missions already completed on someone else’s playthrough. Another horrible thing is that even when playing alone the game constantly needs an online connection. If for any reason you lose it for one second, you will get kicked and lose any unsaved progress. This is unacceptable, if I’m playing alone there should be no reason to stop me from going offline.

Technically speaking, the game is plagued by many problems: textures not loading or taking too long to load, enemies glitching inside walls or suddenly spawning close to you, enemies walking backwards, objects floating mid-air, dead bodies changing their position, hero t-posing in the character menu, crouch and start button no longer working (on controller), parts of the world feeling empty and much more. It seems like the game was heavily rushed for release, which is also visible with the poor performance. It doesn’t matter what settings you change, you won’t notice any frame-rate difference but you will often get frame drops that will ruin your experience. The game also includes Denuvo anti-tamper, which may be the cause of some problems.


[table]
    [tr]
        [th] ✅ Pros [/th]
        [th] ❌Cons [/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td]
• Gunplay improvements for an Arkane game (thanks to ID Software)

• Fascinating setting and detailed interiors
[/td]
        [td]
• Bland story and secondary characters

• Cheap images as cutscenes

• Always online (even when playing alone)

• One of the worse AI in videogames

• No public matchmaking and bad co-op progression

• Horrible stealth implementation

• Impressive quantity of technical issues

• Poor optimization and Denuvo anti-tamper
[/td]
[/tr]
[/table]


[h1]Verdict: 6/10[/h1]
Despite a bland story, horrible cutscenes and lack of interesting characters, Redfall could be a sufficiently enjoyable co-op experience if you like the setting and can wait for all the technical issues to be fixed (as well a substantial price-drop). The always-online requirement must be removed, online matchmaking must be added, the co-op progression must be expanded, and the optimization must be improved. Right now it is impossible to really recommend Redfall with all these issues and the insane price, but this is still an Arkane game, even if it’s the worst one they’ve made to date.

Performace has a lot to work on, but generally I find it really fun to play and usually average about 60fps@1440p High settings with a 6700XT and 3600X paired with 32GB@3200MHz.

The gameplay loop is addictive, the missions are serviceable, and it's a nice co-op romp.

Some of you might’ve thought I was silly for giving Redfall a positive review when it first came out — especially with its original price tag. But I didn’t just judge it by launch day. I looked ahead, saw the potential, and I’m proud to say I still stand by that decision. And now? I’m SO proud they changed the game price — a big step in the right direction.

Let’s talk positives first:
Redfall nails multiplayer and interaction. It’s got that classic co-op magic — from hoarding loot and exploring every corner of the map to laughing at weird glitches or strategizing through chaotic fights. The story is strong, with a sort of retro Left 4 Dead vibe and killer cutscenes that feel like they belong in a comic book. There are tons of skins for characters and weapons, multiple difficulty levels, and a satisfying level-up and ability system. No two characters or enemies feel the same, and I love how you’re constantly stumbling into random encounters around the map. The combat even lets you shoot while downed (which saves lives more than you’d think), and characters have unique voice lines that make them feel alive. You can dodge attacks, and yes — sliddeee.

Now the not-so-great stuff:
The original pricing was definitely rough, and only one save slot per person is really limiting, especially when you want to restart a character. Some guns can’t be accessorized (missed opportunity), and the intro screen is not only boring — it’s loud. There's lag in some areas, which will likely be fixed in time, and it’s a little annoying that you have to check the missions tab to see if something is complete. I also really wish we could decorate the safe house — there’s so much potential there. And for my Remi mains: it would be awesome if her launch pads could double as explosives.

Graphics-wise, if you like that gritty, stylized retro vibe from Left 4 Dead, this is your lane. And while the story already brings a lot to the table (with a few light puzzles), I’d love to see even more side quests you discover naturally instead of everything starting at your safe place.

Having said this, I've still found some entertaining gameplay value in this title. For example, the stealth mechanics are barebones but still make for some interesting combat options. The gunplay and the mechanics of the guns feels great but it's mired by an odd UI inventory system; there are moment of genuine eeriness when haunting voices coming from another room chant "the blood the blood the blood the blood the blood", but after a couple of hours, it gets stale.

I am hoping that this game will get better because it's too late for a refund, so I suppose the TLDR: absolutely avoid this game until it's deeply discounted.

reviews.review: Nothing original. Routine gore comedy. The gore value is supposed to give the viewer a trendy feeling. But there's nothing new here. Therapy scene was stolen from Austin Powers but with more gore of course. Silly fighting scenes, the usual underdog antihero guy who finds a girl he likes. Silly mafia villains. Hollywood thinks very lowly of it's audience. I like Nicholas Cage but other than a cliched silly Dracula with too much gore makeup and bad teeth, he adds very little here. Nicholas Hoult is the sympathetic guilty-victim. His part is thin with a very silly superpower boost. There's implied depth to his character but nothing of any substance in the script. At best a one time view for curiosity. The game thinks of much more than it is.

At the time/price of writing, this game is not worth $70. I went into the game aware that the campaign was fairly short compared to other games in this genre and price range, and was fully prepared to accept the 20ish hours of curated content for a decent endgame cycle. And that's where it finally lost me... This is the first looter/shooter I've ever played that has ABSOLUTELY NO ENDGAME CONTENT, a topic that seemed deceitfully avoided prior to release.

I'd change this to a positive review with a free update that adds, at least, something to do after the campaign other than doing it again... or half my money refunded.

Spent a good amount of time doing all the missions, looking for collectibles etc. Here's my thoughts after completing the campaign.

PROS

Good atmosphere
Good soundtrack 
Solid story, I liked the ending
Combat is solid
Staking vampires is incredibly satisfying, does not get old. 


CONS

A number of strange and just plain dumb design choices. The world is open, but not really. You have to be on the specific missions for things like keys to spawn. There's no real point in exploring if you arent on the correct mission.
There are two maps, but after you finish the first one, you can't go back. When you finish the final mission, the game ends and you are forced to do NG+. You cannot go back for side missions or collectibles.
The collectibles are ridiculously tedious. They are very well hidden and you cannot track them.
The talent tree has tiers, you have to save points for higher levels so you end up saving a lot of points. 
The AI gets stuck on things and is pretty dumb in general.
Why are lock picks limited? Why is not just an unlocking mini game? 

Overall, fun if you like the core gameplay loop but very rough. Certainly not worth $70. 6.5/10

[b]Short answer:[/b] If the game piques your interest, then get it on deep sale. I had a decent amount of fun with it at times, but I can't picture even a fully-patched [i]and[/i] enhanced version of this game that is worth its $70 price tag. The price is pretty insulting in its launch state.

[b]Long answer:[/b] There's a decent shooter here buried beneath a mountain of bugs, an uninteresting story, and some questionable design decisions.

The guns are pretty satisfying in both sound and feel, and their power generally feels significant so long as you keep up with the looter shooter grind by replacing your favorites frequently with their higher-numbered counterparts. Think Borderlands with a much more conservative number of items to sift through. I appreciate the streamlining. The game is also generally good at providing a decent number of fast travel points, preventing the fatigue of running all the way across a zone.

But that's where the good stuff ends for me. That traversal is actually slowed greatly by red mist scattered generously throughout the map, and which can only be eliminated (temporarily) by shooting a target with a specific weapon type--one which you may not generally bother having equipped. You'll either have to open the cumbersome menu to swap out weapons in one of your (extremely conservative) three slots, or use one of a few of the characters' traversal mechanics on a very long cooldown in order to bypass the red mist. By the way, the game [i]doesn't[/i] pause when you're in menus, even when you're playing solo. (I understand the developers are supposed to be working on an offline mode that I assume will actually behave like a proper single-player game, but it is not ready as of the time I'm reviewing it.)

Beyond the frustrations of movement, there are numerous game-breaking bugs. You will find progress thwarted by immortal enemies or key items falling outside of reachable space. You might get booted from the game even when playing alone because you lost connection to a server. These are things that can theoretically be patched, but the rate of development being done on the game post-launch is (so far) not encouraging, so I wouldn't hold my breath waiting for fixes.

Even if you somehow dodge bugs, you'll be faced with a predictable, fairly boring story accompanied by uninteresting fetch quests that clearly try to tug at your heart strings. And speaking of fetch quests, you'll often find yourself having to scour every inch of a building to find the magic collection of pixels representing an item you need to progress. At times, it's infuriating.

Redfall will waste your time in numerous ways. There's some decent combat with some heavily-repeated enemy types in there, but the story is unremarkable and the map is somehow even more frustrating to traverse than Borderlands' open, empty spaces (on top of having plenty emptiness of its own).

I was awaiting this game because I'm easy to please when it comes to vampire games, and had planned to play it with a friend. While I had fun with my friend, this is not really difficult : having fun when playing coop is dumb easy, as long as there is a vague gameplay.

Still, the fun I had killing enemies with terrible AI doesn't make the flaws of the game less apparent. But the real shame is that it could have been so much better. There are ideas beneath the pile of blandness. The bits in "memories" have interesting visuals, for instance, that hint at environments that could have been spectacular to play through. Some skills are somewhat amusing to use.

But... this just doesn't come close to being enough. Also, the storytelling is terrible : why so much text, in my fast action-paced shooter ? Who's got time to read tons of diary entries or letters ? Why do the memories kill the pace so much too ?

The enemies : not very varied. Four or five types of vampires, and cultists that all act the same (shoot you), and they take a crazy long time to react to having you in front of them.

We played in highest difficulty and took less than 12 hours to finish, while doing all the side quests we found on our way and liberating all safehouses we found.

All the time I found myself comparing this game with another, far superior "Coop FPS with set characters and quests" : Borderlands. And Borderlands is better in all regards :
- Fun, varied weapons
- Varied builds
- Amusing quests
- Entertaining dialogs
- Broad type of enemies

This is not worth 70€. I had much higher expectations of Arkane and it's a shame they delivered this.

If you want to play a coop shooter, just buy Borderlands instead.

A lot of people here complain about the game being empty and the AI being dumb and yes, the AI is absolutely lobotomised. Some simple changes to normal enemy behaviour, such as seeking cover, reacting to allies dying and faux flanking would give them a lot more life. I always liked how the AI in the Division 2 functioned in their open world.
The vampires are fine. They jump around chaotically and hit you. 

I actually like that the town of Redfall is largely abandoned. Its creepy. A few more random events here and there, aside from faction encounters could be fun though. Again, a lot can be taken from the Division 2 playbook. D2 was formulaic, but full of stuff to do.

The artstyle and the athmosphere work great together. If the environment was a bit more dynamic, with rain, wind or even storms, it would elevate the experience even more. I love the vampires. They are always gloating, they wear high collars and have slicked back hair. The fact that you have to stake them to kill them. Just great. Even the human factions are kinda interesting, but they don't really function differently. Cultists have poison grenades and PMCs have turrets. Thats pretty much it.  
Guns are strange. The animations and sounds are serviceable, even cool sometimes, but aiming feels... swimmy? Might be my settings though.

So me personally, I can spend a lot of time in this game. It works for me, even if its absolutely halfbaked. I can definitely understand a lot of the negative feedback, but this game can still be repaired, if technical fixes and additions to content can be expected.

It's good fun, don't believe the anti-hype. 

The art is GLORIOUS and the world-building is thick and rich. The playable characters interact with one another in an organic fashion, and have charming conversations. There's a metroidvania feel to exploring the world of Redfall, as you unlock various areas and become strong enough to go to new places and face new enemies.

Certainly not without its issues currently. The combat feels a bit stiff, and mouse aiming can feel sluggish when switching to it from other games. The ability to collect items and notes can be hampered or delayed at times. The player skills and powers are a bit lacklustre for now, and thus can be easy to forget.

Recommended to enjoy the game with your usual co-opmates, don't take it too seriously. It's not L4D, but it's not meant to be. It's an open world vampire-killing exploration story, with spiritual references to a bunch of games, and pure Arkane blood running through its veins.

Reccomended also to let them iron out some bugs, tighten up the meta, and tweak the performance before you pass your final judgement. Currently it's not AAA but it definitely has the potential, and I have strong faith that it will get to where it should be after a few patch cycles. 

Remember the Bethesda bug curse, and the pandemic that knocked a lot of projects around.

Overall recommended; if you can look past the launch clumsiness, find yourself a nice discount somewhere, and are willing to stick with the game through a few growing pains, I think you'll enjoy the world of Redfall.

It really is that bad, if not worse.

Without reiterating everything you've probably seen in every other negative review,
the simplest way to put it is just that the game is a loveless, hollow, clunky mess.
Not even a 'So bad it's good', just plain bad and embarrassingly so.

I wouldn't even buy this game for $20, let alone a full $70.

The AI is so dumb that on the highest difficulty you can play at start, the first vampire I faced did no damage to me. Then I faced two, and killed them without a hit. The AI does nothing but run into your gun, and it's just ... not fun.

Loving the game so far. I have been stealthily exploring every building, trailer park and neighborhood in between missions. The ambiance and feel of the world is great if you take the time to look around and enjoy it. I like how the story is being told so far through not just the story line missions but also through other means found while exploring. For myself the game looks and sounds great with the exception of the occasional FPS stuttering. It does have a few issues that I feel need some attention. First and foremost is the enemy AI. About 30% of the encounters I have had feel very fluid and action packed. While the other 70% of encounters have felt like I am either playing Whack-a-Mole or red light, green light with the enemy. They will just stand there for 3-6 seconds and look at you. Once you start shooting them, they might start looking confused and walking around like Pres. Biden trying to leave a stage or they may just stand there and take their death.  My second issue is the lack of match making. I can't really understand how that was never implemented to start with as it is pretty standard for today's games. I don't just friend everyone that I come into contact with while gaming. So with a smaller group of friends, getting a group together is kind of a pain in the butt. Hence the reason I haven't spoken to how any of the group game play feels. I am really looking forward to whats to come with further updates and expansions for Redfall. 

PS: For everyone whining about the cost being $70 USD - $100 USD. Get over it. It's called inflation. If you don't understand that or if you don't like how much something costs, simply don't buy it and move on.

Ok, the negative reviews are a bit harsh. Give the game a chance. It is like Secret World and Dishonored had a child game. I am enjoying the game play and have no technical issues. I have run into a couple gun fights where the enemy hit box is very small. Overall, I like the atmosphere and theme. looking forward to the game being optimized. Net net, breath and enjoy the game this software company tried to develop. Over time it will be as good as Dishonored. Side note, for those that complain about the exaggerated characters features then I guess you never played a Dishonored game. Before you judge please take into consideration that it take a lot for a game studio to develop a game. For me the Dishonored style of character is awesome & different. I really wanted to like this game.  I liked the Dishonored games and loved Prey, so I assumed I would get something along those lines and pre-ordered.  What I got instead was:

1) An open world with virtually nothing interesting to discover
2) A game with essentially 2 different enemies to kill endlessly 
3) character choices whose abilities barely have an impact on gameplay
4) Miniboss encounters so poorly designed that you can 1-2 shot them before they even make a move.
5) a set of two types of quests (fetch and kill this miniboss/boss)

It's pretty and it was fun for about the first two hours, until you realize the aforementioned points.  Don't spend more than $15 for this game.

The story is simple because its a looter shooter. Don't expect super in depth character development because that is not this games purpose. Do I think this game is Game of the Year material? Absolutely NOT but that doesnt make it any less fun to just run around kill some vampires with some friends.
For all the flaws this game has, I've had a ton of fun playing it. It's better in groups, and probably should have been priced at $40 for what you get.

It's a genuinely fun game so far, especially enjoyable for date night or spending time with the partner. Would I pay $70 again for it? No, but I think it would be worth a solid $40-50. I think the negative reviews are a little too harsh and are blaming Arkane for what has sadly become widespread industry practice.

reviews.review:
I got Redfall for free through GPU purchase. Even free I would not recommend it.

Redfall, coming from Arkane hurts in a special way. It doesn't feel like a AAA game, it doesn't play like a AAA game, it isn't even the size or length of a AAA game... It definitely doesn't feel or play like an Arkane game. Looking at the pricetag of it actually makes me sick to think that they thought this was acceptable to release at that price point... Or at all...

For reference, my first boss encounter lasted about 10 seconds. I don't know who tf this game is for.

Stay far away from this game, if you value your money AT ALL, do NOT purchase this title... This one is a dud.
It's VERY hard to believe that the same studio gave us PREY and Dishonored 2.
I'm beyond pissed that i spent 100 bucks on this game.  Y'all ripped me off.  I seriously thought it would be worth it because Arcane/Bethesda but y'all played me.  Never again.

Overpriced for what it delivers.  No animated cut scenes, boring in game storytelling.  AI is easy to beat on Midnight difficulty (you have to beat the game to get the next difficulty up, so I don't know if that is a challenge). World is mostly empty.  Pretty sure they only had one animator working on this because non of the npcs move.  Nice atmospheric effects and lighting, but you need a pretty hefty rig to run the game.

I haven't encountered any game breaking bugs or the game being unplayable. However all my hardware is brand new. This game game on gamepass, but I was given a free copy with my RTX4080 purchase. 

I have noticed small bugs and glitches however, but none to what players are torching it over. In all honesty with the unfortunate push to meet release dates, it's become just a normality to release games and patch them later. Expecting a PC game to play perfectly on launch date is unrealistic these days.

Overall haven't had any game breaking problems and I've enjoyed the game overall don't think it should be $70 though.

I hope after some updates it will be perceived well I enjoy it and I want more content to come of this game in the future.

Massive performance issues with constant FPS nosedives, frequent connection issues, connection issues leading to progression loss on characters, and virtually no actual content.   This doesn't even deserve to have been an Early Access release, let alone final release.   I would refund this if Steam would allow it.

Edit, since we can't respond to Bethesda responses:   I'm on a Ryzen 7950x w/3070 TI, a pro-series NVME drive.   There is no spec issue here.   This is running at 4k on moderate settings with DLSS and consistently 130+ FPS--except for the very, very frequent nosedives in performance.

I want a refund, period.
